overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the OML by discussing an unposted shellfish topic, since the chair did not reasonably anticipate it, declined to review the public hearing claim, and noted the vague "Old Business" posting was insufficient. No order issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board adopted a new shellfish regulation at its Sept. 13, 2011 meeting although the topic was not on the posted agenda.
allegations.key_passage: Following our review, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by discussing a topic during its meeting that was not included in the meeting notice because the chair did not reasonably anticipate that discussion on this topic would occur.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board did not hold a public hearing before adopting the new shellfish regulation.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern when a public body must hold a public hearing; therefore we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Not raised by the complainant: the AG noted the posted 'Old Business' agenda topic, under which the memorandum was discussed, was too vague to give notice.
allegations.key_passage: we note that the topic "Old Business" on the Board's agenda, under which Sgt. Lowney's memorandum was discussed, was insufficiently detailed for purposes of the Open Meeting Law.
